follow100Note: Of the $15.38 kept as profit per $100 of revenue, $15.40 accrued to Uber shareholders, because non-controlling partners absorbed a small loss. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Net income of $1,774M includes a $2M loss attributable to non-controlling interests; $1,776M is attributable to Uber shareholders (the $0.83 EPS figure).

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs a $0.32 loss a year ago

oneTimers: Net income includes a $51M net benefit (pre-tax) from revaluations of Uber's equity investments.

Income taxes were a $402M benefit this quarter rather than an expense — almost all of it deferred (deferred income taxes were a $412M benefit in the cash-flow statement) — so reported net income came in above pre-tax income.
otherDetail: Other income (expense), net of $262M, less $105M of interest expense and a $13M loss from equity method investments.

segments.name: Mobility
segments.note: Rides — the original Uber business. Gross Bookings rose 13% to $21.2B.

segments.name: Delivery
segments.note: Food and grocery delivery — Uber Eats and couriers. Gross Bookings rose 15% to $20.4B.

segments.name: Freight
segments.note: Trucking logistics — matching shippers with carriers. Revenue and bookings each slipped 2%.

takeaways.text: Trips grew 18% to 3.0 billion and Gross Bookings 14% to $42.8B, with Monthly Active Platform Consumers up 14% to 170 million. Revenue rose 14% to $11.5B — Mobility +15%, Delivery +18%, Freight −2%.
takeaways.title: Trips kept climbing

takeaways.text: Income from operations rose to $1,228M from just $172M a year ago, as revenue grew 14% while total costs and expenses rose only about 3%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 35% to $1.9B — 4.4% of Gross Bookings, up from 3.7%.
takeaways.title: Operating profit took off

takeaways.text: Operating cash flow and free cash flow were both $2.3B in the quarter. Uber ended March with $6.0B of unrestricted cash and short-term investments, and guided Q2 Gross Bookings to $45.75–47.25B.
takeaways.title: Cash flow matched profit

verdict: Uber grew revenue 14% to $11.5B as trips rose 18% to 3.0 billion, and operating profit jumped to $1.2B from $172M a year ago — a $402M tax benefit then lifted net income to $1.8B.
